Vijay Laxmi Dwivedi And Another vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others
on 9 July, 2024
Author: Saumitra Dayal Singh

Bench: Saumitra Dayal Singh
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:111298-Db
Court No. - 39
Case :- Writ - C No. - 35482 of 2016
Petitioner :- Vijay Laxmi Dwivedi And Another
Respondent :- State Of U.P. And 2 Others

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Petitioner :- Shiv Kumar Pal,Amit Kumar,Arun Kumar Mishra,Harbansh Prasad Pa Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.,Mahboob Ahmad,Ravi Anand Agarwal,Shachindra Kumar Mishr Hon'ble Saumitra Dayal Singh,J.
Hon'ble Donadi Ramesh,J.

1. Heard Sri Vindeshwari Prasad along with Sri Amit Kumar, learned counsel for the petitioners,
Shri Shachindra Kumar Mishra, learned counsel for respondent nos.3, 4 and 5 and Sri Arimardan Singh Rajpoot, learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel for the State.
2. Present writ petition has been filed for the following reliefs:
"(i) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of certiorari quashing the impugned order dated 15/16.01.2015 passed by the respondent no.2 (Annexure No.4 to the writ petition).
Vijay Laxmi Dwivedi And Another vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187214963/
1
(ii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus commanding the respondents to hand back / restore the land of the petitioners free with their right as land holders."

3. Undeniably, public work of vital importance to the society has been executed wherein some part of the land of the petitioners has been utilized for the purpose of setting up Thermal Power Plant at Village Lohgara, Tehsil Bara, District Allahabad.

Though the Power Plant has been set up on another land (not belonging to the petitioners), but on their land bearing Plot Nos.207 M and 208 M admeasuring 148 square meters, underground pipeline is described to have been laid to run the Power Plant.
The total area of the land is admeasuring 0.0320 acres and 0.0233 hectacres.
4. Initially, proceedings were drawn for temporary acquisition of the land of the petitioners along with portions of Plot No.122 Ka M, 151 M, 152 M and 173 M.
That temporary acquisition was proposed for one year.

Documentation has been shown to exist that such temporary acquisition first arose on 10.12.2012 under notice issued under Section 35 of the Land Acquisition Act by Special Land Acquisition Officer, Allahabad.
5. Then it is an admitted fact, after laying the pipelines, the land was levelled and attempted to be handed over to the petitioners.
Existence of the pipelines laid at depth of 1.7 meters is admitted to the respondents.
It is also not in dispute that the respondents require the said pipelines and are utilizing the same to supply water to Thermal Power Plant.
6. With respect to the acquisition made, earlier another Writ-C No.10887 of 2013 Dinesh Vs. State of U.P. and others was filed by third party.

entities.text: Writ-C No.10887 of 2013 Dinesh Vs. State of U.P. and others
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: That was dismissed by the following order dated 28.02.2013:
"Heard Sri Rahul Mishra, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner, learned counsel for the State and Sri Mahboob Ahmad learned counsel appearing for the respondents.
The petitioner in this writ application challenges the temporary acquisition made under Section 35 of the Land Acquisition Act for the purpose of lying down underground pipeline over his plot.
Section 35 clearly provides that temporary acquisition can be made for public purpose and the period of acquisition shall not be more than three years.
The maximum period prescribed under Section 35 has not expired.
Lying down the pipe line is for supply of water for running a Power Plant

,
therefore, the acquisition is for the public purpose.
In view of that, we find no justification to accept the prayer of the writ application.

The writ application is dismissed."
7.

So far as the present petitioners are concerned, they filed Writ-C No.39803 of 2014 which was disposed of by the following order dated 04.08.2024:
Vijay Laxmi Dwivedi And Another vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187214963/

entities.text: Vijay Laxmi Dwivedi And Another vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2 "Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, learned Standing Counsel for respondents no. 1, 2 & 3 and Sri Mahboob Ahmad, learned counsel appearing for respondent no. 4 and 5.

A similar grievance had been raised in Writ C No. 45678 of 2013 which petition was disposed of in the following terms:
"Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, learned counsel for the State and the learned counsel for the respondent no.5 Prayag Raj Power Generation Company Ltd.,
Bara, district Allahabad.

entities.text:
Prayag Raj Power Generation Company Ltd.,
Bara,
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Petitioners are aggrieved with the award dated 14.05.2013 contained in Annexure 9.

According to the petitioners the rate and amount of compensation determined for payment to the landholders is inadequate even for temporary occupation in terms of section 35 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

The other grievance raised on behalf of the petitioners is that temporary occupation will not be for one year and their lands are liable to remain under full or partial occupation for longer years because the authorities have plans to lay down pipelines for supply of water through lands of the petitioners and there is every likelihood that even after the period of one year of temporary occupation is over, the authorities will not remove the water pipelines.

So far as grievance with regard to the rate of compensation, it has rightly been pointed out by the learned counsel for the State and for the private respondents that petitioners have efficacious remedy by seeking reference to Civil Court under sub section (3) of Section 35 of the Act.

So far as other apprehension of the petitioners is concerned, we expect the authorities to act in accordance with law and ensure that if the lands have been taken over only for the purpose of temporary occupation, the same should be handed back to the land holders who will be free with their land rights as landholders.
In case such right is to be adversely effected then the authorities would be well advised to work out a mutual acceptable solution.
Writ petition is accordingly disposed of."

We dispose of this writ petition on the same terms."
8.
That order has attained finality.

The petitioners have not raised any plea against and in any case they have not succeeded against permanent nature of the acquisition made inasmuch as they have not filed any petition to restrain the respondents to lay pipelines to run the Power Plant.

9. Then we are aware of the earlier order passed in this proceeding on 09.08.2018, reads as below:
"The land of the petitioners was acquired for a temporary purpose for laying down the pipe line only for a period of one year but the possession thereof has not been restored.

Vijay Laxmi Dwivedi And Another vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187214963/
3

entities.text: Vijay Laxmi Dwivedi And Another vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners by means of this petition inter-alia demand the land should be restored to them.

The Court vide order dated 02.08.2016 had directed the District Magistrate to file his personal affidavit to show cause under what authority he has referred the dispute to the Court, when the issue before him was with regard to restoration of the land in favour of the petitioners after the expiry of the temporary acquisition.
The affidavit of the District Magistrate only states that the land was handed to the petitioners after levelling the land.
It does not specify the manner in which the possession of land was restored to the petitioners and the date of redelivery of possession.
Learned Standing Counsel is directed to file an affidavit of the District Magistrate clearly stating the date on which the land was redelivered to the petitioners.
The District Magistrate shall also pay the compensation as determined for the said temporary acquisition against which a reference has been made before the District Judge.

It is only after the order determining the compensation is produced before the petitioners that they may demand reference to the District Judge for determining the adequate compensation if they are not satisfied.
The District Magistrate may clarify all the above aspects of the matter within two weeks.
List thereafter."

10. In compliance to that order, the impugned order has been passed by the District Magistrate,
Prayagraj, whereby it has been disclosed that the reference for determination of compensation for temporary acquisition has been made to the Court of learned District Judge, Prayagraj, the same has been challenged in this proceeding.
11. Thus it cannot be denied that the land of the petitioners has been utilized for public purpose of laying of underground pipeline (in depth 1.7 meters) to run a Thermal Power Plant.
The pipeline may have been installed in 2012 and it is still existing.
Those pipelines cannot be dismantled without disturbing or impeding functioning of the Thermal Power Plant itself.

12. Even otherwise, it being undisputed to the respondent that they have laid the underground pipeline on the land belonging to the petitioners, they cannot be said to have made temporary acquisition of the petitioners' land.
By very nature, temporary acquisition would not only involve possession of the land being returned to the land owner but restoration of its nature without any permanent change made to it.
Once underground pipeline has been laid under the land belonging to the petitioners, it can never be said that the respondents made temporary acquisition of the land.
To the extent, they have altered the nature and utilization of the land and its prospective use, alteration made is permanent.

Vijay Laxmi Dwivedi And Another vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187214963/
4 13.

entities.text: Vijay Laxmi Dwivedi And Another vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: We are also aware that other co-sharers of the petitioners may have entered into sale deed with respondent nos.4, 5 and 6 whereas no such sale deed has been entered into by the petitioners.

14. In view of the above, interest of justice would be met if fair compensation is paid to the petitioners for loss of their rights over the land, in proportion to their ownership rights over the same.
Also, the petitioners would remain entitled to compensation for temporary acquisition of the land disclosed for period of one year, which has continued till now.

Thus the petitioners would remain entitled for temporary acquisition for the period 10.12.2012 to 30.06.2024.
15.

At this stage, learned counsel for the respondents has placed reliance on the Government Order dated 19.03.2015 that provides for constitution of the appropriate Committee by District Magistrate to compute due compensation where land acquisition proceedings may not have been initiated, in accordance with law.

16. Keeping in mind the above Government Order, the writ petition is disposed of with the following directions:
(i) District Magistrate, Prayagraj shall make further reference to the Court of learned District Judge, Prayagraj to compute due compensation to the petitioners for temporary acquisition of the land for the entire period 10.12.2012 to 30.06.2024,
within next two weeks.

entities.text: Court of learned District Judge, Prayagraj
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
(ii) Subject to a copy of this order being place before the learned District Judge,
Prayagraj, the pending and the new reference made by the District Magistrate,
Prayagraj may be dealt with and decided as expeditiously as possible, preferably with a period of three months from the date of compliance made by the District Magistrate.

(iii) Also, the District Magistrate, Prayagraj may constitute an appropriate committee in terms of Government Order dated 19.03.2015 to compute the fair compensation together with due interest etc. for permanent acquisition of the land owned by the petitioners namely 148 Sq. Meters of Plot Nos.207M and 208M, as on 01.07.2024.

(iv) All amount of compensation be computed and paid to the petitioners within a period of six months subject to the petitioners executing appropriate sale deed in favour of the respondents, against payment of that compensation.
We are conscious that the normal period of temporary acquisition of three years elapsed in the past.

However, a provision for payment of compensation for continued temporary acquisition has been made, in the interest of justice.
17.

It is further made clear that this order shall have no bearing or effect on any compensation already paid to the co-sharers who already have executed sale deed and with respect to whom rights have attained finality.
